The observation is right and the fix is wrong, so this is REFUTED with the fix corrected. What is right: driving lately.html in chromium, .xaxis span is flex:1 1 0 with white-space:normal, and at 768 the five shown ticks measure 27 Apr=2 lines, 18 May=2, 8 Jun=1, 29 Jun=2, 13 Jul=2 — exactly the ragged mix the seat names, axis height 14.84px -> 29.69px (+14.85px, the claimed 15px). What is wrong. (1) The band. The ragged/wrapped condition is NOT 'between 560 and 900'. Measured line counts by width: one line at >=1145; ragged 1140 down to ~1045; uniform two-line 1045-901; one line again 900 down to 793 (at <=900 the hero stacks to one column, so the plot is at its WIDEST — colW 54.5px at 900, wider than the 53.5px at 1440); ragged again 792-~705; uniform two-line ~705-390. So the seat missed an entire desktop band (901-1140, a normal laptop window and any half-screen split on a 2560 display) and named as broken the one band, 800-900, that is actually clean. (2) The fix breaks the axis outright. `.xaxis span` is a flex item with default min-width:auto; adding white-space:nowrap raises its min-content width to 45.55px, so the twelve ticks can no longer shrink with the plot. Measured with the seat's rule injected: the .xaxis row overflows its container by 209px at 901, 62px at 700, 122px at 640 and 252px at 390 — every tick loses alignment with the column it labels and the row spills outside the hero card. The opacity:0 half does not rescue it, because opacity:0 items still occupy their 45.55px min-width; the seat's right-aligned :last-child would render roughly 250px off the right edge of the card at 390. (3) The thinning is in the wrong place and thins too far: it strips twelve ticks to two across 900-390, i.e. precisely where the ruler has the most room (900-793 needs no help at all), while leaving 901-1140 ragged. Two anchors also delete the midpoint, which is what lets a reader place a column in time at a glance. (4) It breaks the first-run state: that frame renders `
13 Jul
` (one span). :first-child and :last-child both match it, last wins, and the single tick jumps from centred over its one column to right-aligned at <=900. Severity confirmed as defect, not raised: the ruler is visibly ragged and the card grows ~15px, but the chart still reads and nothing untrue is asserted.
breaks: The seat's version as written breaks the axis-to-column alignment and pushes the row up to 252px past the plot at 390, and right-aligns the first-run single tick. The sharpened version's risks are narrower: display:none removes the .mute spans from the flow in the thinned bands, so anything that indexes .xaxis span positionally (nothing does today — the tooltip and keyboard model bind to .colw inside .plot, not to ticks) would need checking; the .sr paragraph still carries all twelve week labels, so the screen-reader account of the axis is unchanged and the honest-degradation contract is untouched. Re-measure after it lands: axis height at 1440/1141/1140/901/900/793/792/768/560/390 (must stay 14.8px everywhere); hero card total height at 768 and 390 (drops ~15px, so the shots at 768x1024 and 390x844 must be recaptured, and any layout assertion in interaction-check.mjs keyed to hero height re-run); document scrollWidth at 390 (must equal clientWidth); and audit.mjs, since the type ramp and leading are unchanged but the frame set is not.
